 FAQs
 Will This Group 24 Lithium Battery Fit My Existing Group 24 Battery Box?
 Will This Group 24 Lithium Battery Fit My Existing Group 24 Battery Box?
 Yes. We designed this group 24 lithium battery around the standard Group 24 footprint, so it fits the battery space commonly used by Group 24 lead-acid and AGM batteries. It is especially practical for RVs, travel trailers, boats, and other setups where you want to move to LiFePO4 without rebuilding the existing battery compartment.
 Can I Use My RV Converter With This 12V 100Ah Lithium Battery?
 Can I Use My RV Converter With This 12V 100Ah Lithium Battery?
 A converter or charger with a LiFePO4 charging profile is the right match for this 12V 100Ah lithium battery. Our recommended AC charging setup uses a 14.6V LiFePO4 charger; if your RV still uses an older lead-acid-only converter, upgrading the charging section or adding a dedicated LiFePO4 charger gives the battery the correct charging profile and lets you use its capacity more effectively.
 What Happens If I Charge the Battery Below 32°F?
 What Happens If I Charge the Battery Below 32°F?
 The BMS automatically stops charging when the battery temperature falls below 32°F, protecting the LiFePO4 cells from low-temperature charging damage. This battery does not contain a self-heating system, so when camping in sustained freezing weather, keep the battery compartment insulated or use an external thermostatically controlled battery heater. Charging can resume once the battery warms above the protection threshold.
 Can This Group 24 Marine Battery Start an Outboard Engine?
 Can This Group 24 Marine Battery Start an Outboard Engine?
 No. We designed this group 24 marine battery as a deep-cycle power battery for trolling motors, marine electronics, accessories, and onboard electrical loads, not as an engine starting battery. For equipment requiring high CCA or MCA, use the Vatrer 12V 300Ah  with cranking amps.
 How Long Can This 12V 100Ah Lithium Battery Run a Trolling Motor?
 How Long Can This 12V 100Ah Lithium Battery Run a Trolling Motor?
 A useful estimate is to divide the battery's 100Ah capacity by your trolling motor's average current draw. A motor averaging 20A, for example, gives roughly 5 hours of theoretical runtime, while lower-speed operation can extend that substantially. Wind, current, boat weight, speed, and frequent high-thrust operation all increase energy use, so the Vatrer App is the most practical way to track remaining capacity during a day on the water.
 Why Is Bluetooth Monitoring Better Than a Trolling Motor Battery Gauge?
 Why Is Bluetooth Monitoring Better Than a Trolling Motor Battery Gauge?
 LiFePO4 batteries maintain a relatively flat voltage through much of their discharge cycle, so a basic voltage-based battery gauge can continue to appear nearly full even after significant capacity has been used. Our Bluetooth LiFePO4 battery lets you view SOC and operating data directly through the Vatrer App, giving you a much clearer picture of your remaining power before heading farther from shore or extending an off-grid stay.
 Can This Group 24 Marine Battery Be Installed in a Wet Boat Compartment?
 Can This Group 24 Marine Battery Be Installed in a Wet Boat Compartment?
 Its IP65 ABS housing is designed to resist dust and water exposure, while the moisture-resistant and salt-spray-resistant design adds protection in marine environments. IP65 does not mean the battery is submersible, so mount it above standing bilge water and keep the terminals out of direct water exposure. This gives the battery a protected installation environment while still taking advantage of its marine-oriented enclosure design.
 Can the 150A BMS Run a 2000W Inverter?
 Can the 150A BMS Run a 2000W Inverter?
 A 2000W inverter can be part of the system, but the battery should not be expected to supply a sustained 2000W load. Our 150A BMS supports up to 1920W of continuous load power, so keep the actual continuous load within that rating and size the system cabling and overcurrent protection for the current the battery can deliver. This leaves useful output headroom for common RV appliances and inverter-powered equipment without operating beyond the battery's continuous limit.
 Can I Connect Multiple Group 24 Lithium Batteries for a 24V or 48V System?
 Can I Connect Multiple Group 24 Lithium Batteries for a 24V or 48V System?
 Yes. This group 24 lithium battery supports series and parallel configurations up to 4P4S, allowing a battery bank as large as 51.2V 400Ah. Build multi-battery banks with matching Vatrer batteries, bring them to a similar state of charge before connection, and use balanced cable paths when wiring batteries in parallel. This keeps current sharing more even as you expand an RV, solar, cabin, or backup-power system.
 How Should I Store This Bluetooth LiFePO4 Battery Over Winter?
 How Should I Store This Bluetooth LiFePO4 Battery Over Winter?
 Disconnect loads that could slowly drain the battery during long-term storage and keep it within its specified 14°F to 122°F storage range. The Vatrer App makes it easy to check SOC periodically without relying on an RV panel or voltage gauge. If the battery has been sitting below freezing, let it warm above 32°F before charging; the built-in low-temperature protection will block charging while the battery is too cold.

FAQ
Q: What does Bluetooth of the Group 24 size battery do?
A:

Bluetooth can monitor the Group 24 LiFePO4 battery information, such as battery status, state of charge (SOC), whether it's charging or discharging, voltage, current, power, remaining capacity, temperature, and cycle count. It can also manage the Bluetooth battery's discharge and turn it off.

Q: How do I pair the Group 24 size lithium battery with the Bluetooth application?
A:

To connect the Group 24 battery to Bluetooth, follow these steps:
① Download the Redodo app.  
② Use the Redodo app to scan the QR code on the Group 24 battery.  
Once connected, you can check the status of the battery in real time, including state of charge (SOC), voltage, temperature and more.

Q: Can I connect this 100Ah Group 24 Bluetooth battery to a non-Bluetooth 100Ah Group 24 battery?
A:

It's not recommended to mix different Group 24 battery models. The Bluetooth battery will only display its own data.

Q: What are the differences between the 100Ah Group 24 Bluetooth battery and the non-Bluetooth 100Ah Group 24 battery?
A:

The 100Ah Group 24 Bluetooth battery has a low temperature cut-off and Bluetooth functionality, which helps protect the Bluetooth battery better and allows it to be used in more situations. It can also be easily monitored via an app.

Q: What's the difference between Group 24 Bluetooth battery and Group 31 Bluetooth battery?
A:

The main difference is their dimension.
12V 100Ah Group 24 Bluetooth battery is with dimension: L10.24*W6.61*H8.27 inch, while the 12V 100Ah Group 31 Bluetooth battery is with dimension: L13*W6.77*H8.5 inch.
